_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Jordan covering Natufian culture, Ammonite/Moabite/Edomite kingdoms, Nabataean kingdom (Petra), Roman Decapolis, Byzantine mosaics, Umayyad desert castles, Crusader Kerak/Shobak, Mamluk/Ottoman period, Arab Revolt 1916, British Mandate Transjordan, Hashemite kingdom independence 1946, 1948/1967 wars, Black September 1970, peace with Israel 1994, and regional stability role.

religion.note: Constitutional monarchy with Islamic character; Hashemites are custodians of Al-Aqsa Mosque/Islamic holy sites in Jerusalem; historically tolerant of Christians

ethnic_groups.name: Arab (East Bank Jordanian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous Jordanian tribal communities; Bedouin heritage; Bani Sakhr, Howeitat, Bani Hassan, Adwan; historically backbone of military and monarchy

ethnic_groups.name: Palestinian Jordanian
ethnic_groups.notes: 1948 and 1967 refugees and descendants; hold Jordanian citizenship (unlike most host countries); dominant in commerce; West Bank annexed 1950-1967; 'Jordan is Palestine' debate sensitive

ethnic_groups.name: Iraqi
ethnic_groups.notes: Post-2003 refugees (~500,000 peak); many in Amman; business community; some returned

ethnic_groups.name: Syrian
ethnic_groups.notes: ~1.3 million since 2011; Zaatari camp (world's largest); significant economic and social impact

ethnic_groups.name: Circassian
ethnic_groups.notes: Settled by Ottomans 1878+; Sunni Muslim; Amman/Jerash; serve in Royal Guard; ~120,000

ethnic_groups.name: Chechen
ethnic_groups.notes: Settled same period as Circassians; Zarqa/Azraq; distinct community

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Druze, Turkmen, Dom/Roma)
ethnic_groups.notes: Small Druze community; Dom (Middle Eastern Roma); Egyptian/Filipino workers

country_profile.notes_unique: Petra (UNESCO, New7Wonders); Hashemite dynasty traces lineage to Prophet Muhammad; resource-poor (water scarcity critical); has absorbed more refugees per capita than almost any country; Wadi Rum (Mars filming location)

trade.notes: Qualifying Industrial Zones (QIZ) preferential access to US; garment manufacturing major export; large trade deficit; dependency on oil imports.

infrastructure.notes: Aqaba sole port; Queen Alia international airport hub; high mobile penetration; Aqaba-Amman rail project planned.

governance_indices.notes: Constitutional monarchy with strong royal authority; parliament limited; stable governance; moderate reforms ongoing.

country_profile.national_anthem: As-salam al-malaki al-urduni (The Royal Anthem of Jordan)

geography.terrain: Arid desert plateau east; Great Rift Valley/Jordan Valley west; highlands in between
geography.notes: Occupies strategic location between Middle East and North Africa; Dead Sea is lowest point on Earth; Wadi Rum desert; water-poorest country globally; hosts ~3 million refugees.

economy_extended.notes: Limited natural resources; dependent on foreign aid and remittances; high youth unemployment; IMF reform program; phosphate and potash exports; growing ICT sector.

health.notes: Medical tourism hub; strong healthcare infrastructure; universal coverage for citizens; refugee health burden significant.

food_agriculture.notes: Severely water-scarce; 85% food imports; innovative dryland farming; olive oil production; growing hydroponics sector.

security_stability.notes: High refugee burden (largest per capita); stable monarchy; key Western ally; hosts US military bases; strategic buffer state.

environment_climate.notes: Among world's most water-scarce nations; Disi aquifer depleting; Red Sea-Dead Sea conduit project; ambitious renewable targets; Dana Biosphere Reserve.

demographics_extended.notes: Young population; 70% Palestinian origin; large refugee communities; 'brain drain' of skilled workers; high education levels.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Small open economy; large refugee population (Syrian, Iraqi, Palestinian).

cultural_heritage.national_dish: mansaf (lamb with fermented yoghurt and rice)
major_festivals: Jerash Festival of Culture and Arts
world_heritage_sites: As-Salt – Place of Tolerance and Urban Hospitality
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Jordan Times (English); Al-Rai, Ad-Dustour (Arabic); Jordan TV; moderate press environment by regional standards.
cultural_heritage.notes: Petra (New 7 Wonders); Nabataean heritage; Hashemite Kingdom; Dead Sea; mosaic tradition; Bedouin culture.

energy.notes: One of the most energy-import-dependent countries; rapid solar expansion; Baynouna solar plant; oil shale reserves; planned SMR nuclear.

human_rights_gender.notes: Constitutional monarchy; Article 16 restricts women's rights in personal status; honour crimes concern; refugee hosting strains services.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Civil law (French-influenced); Sharia for personal status
legal_system.notes: Independent judiciary under Constitution; Court of Cassation is highest court; Sharia courts for Muslim personal status; religious courts for Christians.

tourism.notes: Tourism major GDP contributor; Petra one of New 7 Wonders; medical tourism hub; adventure tourism growing.

transport.notes: Aqaba only seaport; Queen Alia airport regional hub; Hejaz Railway heritage; no national rail network currently; road-dependent.

current_leader.name: Abdullah II
current_leader.title: King
current_leader.notes: Hashemite; Sandhurst-educated; balancing act between Israel, Palestinians, and regional powers; modernisation; 'Jordan First'; wife Queen Rania

former_rulers.name: King Abdullah I
former_rulers.notes: Hashemite; son of Sharif Hussein; Emir then King; assassinated at Al-Aqsa Mosque 1951 by Palestinian extremist

former_rulers.name: King Hussein
former_rulers.notes: 46-year reign; survived multiple assassination attempts; Black September (PLO expelled 1970); lost West Bank 1967; peace with Israel 1994; hugely respected; died of cancer February 1999

former_rulers.name: King Talal
former_rulers.notes: Father of Hussein; promulgated liberal constitution 1952; abdicated due to illness
